title: indigo_mount_synscan: a lost UDP reply costs a full 1 s command timeout and lengthens guide pulses
description:
Found on 2026-11-21 on the AZ-GTi (firmware 3.16, UDP over Wi-Fi) by the recorded hardware run of ticket 6a4e8bdf-ff81-4031-8723-df3f84d73b8a: synscan_guide_pulse_accuracy failed in two recorded runs and once alone (RA pulses +816.8 ms, +1148.8 ms, +1242.4 ms too long; limit 400 ms). The driver debug log shows 'No SynScan response before timeout' for a poll command (:j2) and for a pulse command (:I); each lost reply costs the 1 s SYNSCAN_COMMAND_TIMEOUT before the retry, so the end of a guide pulse is delayed by about 1 s, and if the reply to the command ending the pulse is lost the mount physically guides about 1 s longer. A read-only probe of 400 queries lost 2 replies (0.5 %); replies took 9.6 ms median, 19.2 ms maximum. On 2026-11-19 the same case passed 21/21.

To do: decide and implement how the driver retries a UDP command whose reply is lost (shorter per-attempt timeout for UDP, number of attempts, whether serial keeps the present timing; consider commands that are not idempotent and a reply that arrives late and could be taken for the next command's reply), keep guide pulse timing independent of a lost poll reply where possible, model reply loss in the simulator (drop every Nth reply or a named command) and add simulator cases that fail before the change. Bump the driver version. Recorded simulator run and a non-interactive hardware run on the AZ-GTi (no hot-plug). Ticket 6a4e8bdf stays open until a clean recorded hardware run; its harness change is reviewed and independent of this defect.
